item.title: China cuts minimum stock margin requirement to 80%, potentially freeing up 400b yuan in additional funds
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
China cuts minimum stock margin requirement to 80%, potentially freeing up 400b yuan in additional funds China's three stock exchanges announced on Sunday that they will cut the minimum requirement for margin financing from 100 percent to 80 percent, effective November 30, a move that could theoretically free up nearly 400 billion yuan ($56 billion) in additional funds, as regulators seek to stabilize the capital market and bolster investor confidence. The adjustment, approved by the China Securities Regulatory Commission, was announced by the Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing stock exchanges as part of efforts to strengthen countercyclical regulation and promote the stable development of margin financing and securities lending. For example, under the new rules, investors with 1 million yuan in collateral can borrow up to 1.25 million yuan to purchase securities, compared with 1 million yuan previously, increasing their borrowing capacity by 25 percent, according to the Shanghai Securities News. Wang Peng, an associate research fellow at the Beijing Academy of Social Sciences, told the Global Times that the adjustment sends a positive signal of China's determination to stabilize market expectations and strengthen investor confidence. Against the backdrop of declining margin financing balances and subdued trading activity, easing financing requirements could help improve market liquidity, encourage greater participation and provide investors with more flexibility in managing their capital. The move also highlights the flexibility of China's countercyclical capital market regulation, Wang said. Earlier this year, regulators raised the minimum margin requirement to contain excessive leverage and prevent market overheating. The latest reduction reflects a timely response to changing market conditions, demonstrating policymakers' efforts to balance financial risk prevention with sufficient market liquidity. According to the Shanghai Securities News, the margin financing requirement has been at a historically high level, leaving room for a reduction. Starting in the second half of this year, the stock market has retreated sharply from its highs, with margin financing balances and trading activity declining significantly, while overall leverage has remained relatively low. Outstanding margin financing balances stand at about 2.2 trillion yuan, with available collateral estimated at between 500 billion yuan and 1 trillion yuan. Lowering the minimum requirement to 80 percent could release nearly 100 billion yuan in additional financing capacity, and applying the new requirement to existing financing contracts could free up another 300 billion yuan, according to the report. Wang further noted that the adjustment comes as China continues to deepen capital market reforms, encourage long-term investment and improve the market's capacity to serve the real economy. While additional liquidity could support a recovery in market sentiment, sustainable growth ultimately depends on China's economic fundamentals, the quality of listed companies and continued institutional improvements. Strengthening risk management alongside measures to stimulate market activity will be essential to long-term stability, he said. Broader capital market reforms were announced on Sunday. The Shenzhen Stock Exchange began to solicit public feedback on draft rules to introduce a market making mechanism for stocks on its ChiNext board, an initiative aimed at strengthening market stability, resilience and trading quality, according to the Xinhua News Agency. Meanwhile, the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges introduced new fee reductions, including waivers of trading unit usage fees, while extending existing exemptions for listing fees and bond transaction fees by two years through 2028. The China Securities Depository and Clearing Corp Ltd will also extend fee exemptions for certain green, technology innovation and private-sector corporate bonds from January 2027 through December 2028, Xinhua reported. item.title: The world is talking about Shenzhen – what are they talking about?: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
The world is talking about Shenzhen – what are they talking about?: Global Times editorial APEC China 2026. Illustration: Liu Rui/GT Viewed from the world's perspective, Western developed countries are not only observing where China is headed but also reflecting on what they may have missed. Developing nations are examining what kinds of urban lifestyles and industrial development can become a reality, and whether the path to industrialization must necessarily follow the old path of "polluting first, then cleaning up." Shenzhen is not the sole answer to the future, yet it proves there is more than one path forward. Over the past week, Shenzhen has undoubtedly stood at the center of the world's spotlight. In media reports from around the globe - ranging from its densely packed skyscrapers to self-driving taxis on the streets - Shenzhen has been portrayed as a "futuristic city." Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney praised Shenzhen, saying, "The future is designed here, tested here and built here." US President Donald Trump noted that Shenzhen is "clean" and "immaculate," adding that, in contrast, the development and governance of some US cities are "embarrassing." Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori stated that "there is no doubt that we can learn from Shenzhen" in its approach to smart and digital urban governance. On overseas social media platforms, "Shenzhen" continues to dominate the feed. One netizen wrote, "This might be the most futuristic city I've ever visited in my life," while another added, "I wish my country could have a Shenzhen too." Why has a once remote fishing village attracted so much attention? When the world talks about Shenzhen, what exactly are they talking about? Perhaps the answer lies in one word: future. Seen from within China, Shenzhen embodies the concrete form of Chinese modernization, offering a vivid interpretation of the idea that "the next 'China' is still China." When the Special Economic Zone was established in 1980, Shenzhen's population was less than 30,000. Now, it has developed into a modern international metropolis and "super hub" with a population of over 18 million. Today, people here see self-driving cars cruising the streets, drone deliveries becoming part of daily life, robots operating in factories and shopping malls, and companies like Huawei, BYD, DJI, and Tencent making their mark on the global market. Behind these achievements lie China's sustained investment and stable planning - rooted in its own development and oriented toward the future - and, ultimately, a people-centered approach to development. Viewed from the world's perspective, Western developed countries are not only observing where China is headed but also reflecting on what they may have missed. A key reason why Trump's assessment of Shenzhen's roads and urban environment sparked debate in US public opinion is that it touched on the long-standing challenges of urban governance facing American society. Road maintenance, public transportation, and environmental sanitation - these seemingly ordinary public services are, in fact, persistent challenges that many countries struggle to address. Developing nations, meanwhile, are examining what kinds of urban lifestyles and industrial development can become a reality, and whether the path to industrialization must necessarily follow the old path of "polluting first, then cleaning up." Whether developed or developing, countries are beginning to consider whether they should pursue this kind of future. Shenzhen is not the sole answer to the future, yet it proves that there is more than one path forward. Different countries have different historical traditions, cultural practices, resource endowments, and social systems; there can be no single "standard answer" for urban modernization. Nor is Shenzhen's path a template that can be simply replicated. Its significance lies in demonstrating that openness can spur innovation, industry can foster technology, technology can improve lives, and global cooperation can expand the scope for development. Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast remarked, "Shenzhen's transformation reminds us that progress is not a miracle but a resolution." Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, drawing on his experiences from visits in 1998 and 2026, remarked that if someone were to place photographs from then and now side by side, it was almost impossible to believe they were of the same place. This demonstrates that the future can be continuously shaped through reform, opening-up, and relentless exploration. What the world needs is not a replica of Shenzhen, but more cities like Shenzhen that can shape their own futures. Today, Shenzhen has evolved from a place where the Chinese people learned about the world through the "window of the world" to a place where the world observes China and envisions the future. In just over 40 years, Shenzhen has traversed a journey that took some major international metropolises abroad more than a century to complete, proving that modernization does not follow a single predetermined path. A late-developing economy can fully forge its own path - one that balances efficiency with people's livelihoods, and vitality with order. This demonstrates that the "future" is not merely a fixed blueprint. Every country and every civilization can draw upon its own historical traditions, social structures, and resource endowments to find a "future blueprint" that suits it best. British urban planning scholar Peter Hall once wrote Cities of Tomorrow, which traces urban planning practices from the late 19th century to the late 20th century - a work in which London, New York, Paris, and Chicago frequently feature. Today, one "city of tomorrow" after another is emerging across China. We welcome more countries, enterprises, research institutions, and innovators to come to Shenzhen. Rather than merely viewing a single "pre-existing model," we can strive to build more models and explore abundant future forms of AI, green development, urban governance, public services, and industrial cooperation. Shenzhen's story is far from finished, and the exploration of Chinese modernization is still underway. The invitation Shenzhen extends to the world is this: China is willing to showcase its own future, and welcomes the world to bring its own dreams here to jointly create even more bright futures. item.title: China's sector-specific plans map out path to high-quality development
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
China's sector-specific plans map out path to high-quality development BEIJING, Nov. 23 (Xinhua) -- China has rolled out a series of sector-specific plans to translate its broader development vision into concrete action during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), providing detailed roadmaps for key areas of economic and social development. Covering fields ranging from manufacturing and energy to employment, education and health care, the plans set out specific targets, priority tasks and policy measures. Together, they offer a more detailed look at how the world's second-largest economy seeks to cultivate new growth drivers, address emerging development challenges and improve people's livelihoods as it pursues high-quality development amid global uncertainties. FROM BLUEPRINT TO ACTION Five-year plans have long played an important role in China's governance, providing strategic direction and policy continuity for the country's development. The overarching outline of the 15th Five-Year Plan, approved in March this year, sets out the country's overall development objectives through 2030. Sector-specific plans complement this general framework by breaking down national priorities into detailed targets, major projects and implementation arrangements for individual fields. Zhang Linshan, a researcher at the Academy of Macroeconomic Research under the National Development and Reform Commission, said sector-specific plans provide an important basis for guiding development in particular fields, allocating public resources, directing private investment and formulating relevant policies. Several of the recently released plans have established measurable targets for 2030. China's dedicated consumption plan aims to raise total retail sales of consumer goods to around 60 trillion yuan (8.94 trillion U.S. dollars), while the plan for building a new-type power system targets a 50-percent share for non-fossil energy in electricity generation. Other targets include raising average life expectancy to 80 years and reducing carbon dioxide emissions per unit of GDP by 17 percent from the 2025 level, reflecting a focus on both economic development and improvements in people's well-being. BREAKING NEW GROUND A notable feature of the latest round of sector-specific plans is that they cover certain fields for the first time, reflecting China's efforts to address emerging development challenges and respond to changing economic and social needs. Among them is the country's first national-level urban renewal plan, released in May, which calls for the construction and renovation of approximately 770,000 km of urban underground pipelines. The plan also calls for better use of existing land and stronger building safety management, reflecting a shift toward upgrading existing urban areas and improving the quality of urban life. Consumption expansion, disease prevention and control, and cultural heritage protection are among other fields covered by national-level sector-specific plans for the first time. The latest round also includes the first national-level plans dedicated to building China's strengths in finance, sports and tourism. Tian Xuan, dean of Peking University's Guanghua School of Management, said the new plans cover areas crucial to China's economic and social development over the next five years. Their introduction would further improve the country's planning system and help ensure the effective implementation of national development priorities, Tian said. HIGH-QUALITY DEVELOPMENT Beyond their expanding scope, the sector-specific plans share a central objective: advancing high-quality development by strengthening the real economy, fostering innovation and improving people's well-being. A plan to improve industrial foundational capabilities calls for stronger innovation platforms and measures to address weaknesses in key technologies. Another aims to consolidate China's competitive advantages in intelligent connected new energy vehicles and help the country join the ranks of global automotive powerhouses by 2030. Technological innovation is a recurring priority across several sector-specific plans, with measures to promote artificial intelligence applications, breakthroughs in all-solid-state battery technologies and research into frontier technologies. Green transition also features prominently, with plans calling for greener industrial development and closer coordination between electricity supply and computing power. Xin Yongfei, an expert at the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology, said the sector-specific plans coordinate efforts in basic research, technological breakthroughs, commercialization and talent development to build momentum for high-quality development. The pursuit of high-quality development extends beyond industrial upgrading to improving people's livelihoods. The plan for implementing the employment-first strategy calls for promoting employment and entrepreneurship in response to advances in artificial intelligence and expanding job opportunities in services and emerging industries. Other plans seek to improve public services, including expanding enrollment capacity at general senior high schools, developing elderly-friendly communities and expanding access to affordable elderly care services. The plans are also meant to deliver benefits well beyond China's borders, with measures to expand imports of quality foreign products and deepen international cooperation. Koh King Kee, president of the Center for New Inclusive Asia, a Malaysian think tank, said China's sector-specific plans emphasize the development of new quality productive forces and signal a commitment to high-standard opening up and mutually beneficial cooperation. By turning more Chinese demand into development opportunities, the plans will continue to inject much-needed certainty into the global economy, Koh said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: Shoulder the responsibilities of major countries and safeguard world peace
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
Shoulder the responsibilities of major countries and safeguard world peace On Nov. 19, Chinese President Xi Jinping held a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong province. The historic trilateral summit marked the first-ever face-to-face meeting between the Chinese, Russian, and U.S. heads of state, making it a groundbreaking event that will go down in history. Following the summit, the three countries released the China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace, expressing their commitment to maintaining strategic stability and international security. Against a backdrop of global turbulence and uncertainty, the summit further underscored the three countries' resolve to uphold dialogue and manage differences. It helped build consensus on maintaining strategic stability among major countries and safeguarding world peace, while sowing the seeds of building consensus through dialogue, taking responsibilities in meeting challenges, and promoting peace through cooperation. Spanning approximately 90 minutes, the summit drew worldwide attention and reflected the international community's strong desire for peace and stability. Today, changes unseen in a century are accelerating across the globe, geopolitical rivalries are intensifying, and localized conflicts are occurring frequently. With humanity sharing a common destiny, positive interaction among major countries is no longer optional -- it is imperative. Whether in global development, food security, energy security, climate governance, public health cooperation, or global artificial intelligence (AI) governance, coordination and cooperation among major countries are indispensable. Conflicts and disputes continue to erupt around the world, with one hotspot flaring up as another subsides. The international community expects major countries to do more to promote reconciliation and peace talks. As major countries and permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, China, Russia, and the U.S. share common interests in strengthening communication, managing differences, and working together to address global challenges. These expectations align closely with broader international sentiment. At the summit, Xi made four points on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace, calling for mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and dialogue and consultation. Respect is a fundamental principle in major-country interactions. China, Russia, and the U.S. have different national conditions and should respect one another, seek common ground while reserving differences, and pursue shared development. They should respect one another's sovereignty and territorial integrity, the social systems and development paths of their own choice, and their respective core interests and major concerns, while adhering to the principle of non-interference in other countries' internal affairs. Peaceful coexistence is the bottom line for relations among major countries. China, Russia and the U.S. should be partners and friends. They should not go for conflict or confrontation among them, and avoid falling into the "Thucydides Trap." They should bear in mind that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought, and work together to safeguard the postwar international order and uphold the purposes of the UN Charter. Win-win cooperation is another imperative. China, Russia and the U.S. have different development endowments and strong economic complementarity. They can leverage their respective strengths and reinforce one another with what one has to offer. They should firmly oppose decoupling and disruption of industrial and supply chains, and work together to maintain stable and unimpeded energy industrial and supply chains. The three countries should also remain committed to dialogue and consultation, so as to reduce misjudgments, properly manage differences and prevent frictions from escalating. These four points build on one another, charting a course for major countries to pursue peaceful coexistence and development. Their significance extends far beyond the three countries. China adheres to the path of peaceful development. In recent years, China has been promoting the China-Russia comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination for the new era and actively developing the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, with a view to fostering major-country dynamics featuring peaceful coexistence, overall stability and balanced development to the benefit of each other and the world at large. The summit fully demonstrated China's efforts to promote coordination and positive interaction among major countries, as well as its sincerity in managing differences through dialogue and promoting peace and pursuing win-win outcomes through cooperation. "The leaders of these three countries, which are among the most important players on the world stage and are permanent members of the UN Security Council, decided to use the multilateral setting of the APEC summit in Shenzhen to meet face to face, discuss their main concerns, engage in constructive dialogue on issues of common interest, reduce the risk of unintended conflicts arising from strategic miscalculations and curb tensions among the great powers. That in itself is an important diplomatic achievement," said a scholar quoted in an article on the website of Russia's TASS news agency. The U.S. magazine Foreign Affairs observed that the meeting between the three leaders could pave the way for great-power cooperation across ideological lines and stabilize a fragmented world. These international assessments echo China's position and underscore the timeliness and significance of the summit. Viewed from a broad historical perspective, the summit carries even deeper significance for our times. Major countries have always played a uniquely important role in maintaining global strategic stability, safeguarding regional peace, and promoting common development for humanity. Peace among major countries brings stability to the world, while rivalry and confrontation among them can only lead to chaos. More than 80 years ago, China, Russia and the U.S., as key anti-fascist forces in the world, fought shoulder to shoulder and achieved great victories, winning peace and tranquility for the world. The lessons of history remain relevant today: cooperation is the way to jointly withstand risks, while confrontation only breeds disaster. The world today is far from peaceful, with turbulence and conflict intertwined. It is the call of our times and a mission entrusted by history for China, Russia and the U.S. to demonstrate a sense of responsibility, shoulder the responsibilities befitting major countries, and lead and advance multipolarity and greater democracy in international relations. Putin said safeguarding the purposes and principles of the UN Charter and upholding international peace are their shared responsibilities, and they should adhere to the principles of sovereign equality and noninterference in internal affairs, jointly safeguard energy and food security, and strengthen international cooperation on AI governance. Trump said that the summit is a historic event of great importance, drawing global attention. Noting that dialogue is essential to maintaining stability and achieving peace, Trump said all issues should be resolved through dialogue. Some international commentators have simplistically labeled the summit as an example of "great-power condominium" or "Yalta 2.0." Such interpretations essentially apply outdated notions of power politics and the division of spheres of influence to a new form of interaction among major countries in the new era. This misreading ignores both the profound changes in the international landscape and the widespread aspiration of countries around the world to participate in global affairs on an equal footing. The trend toward a multipolar world is irreversible, and bloc confrontation offers no way forward. All parties should take a realistic approach, pave the way for multilateral cooperation, promote common development, and find the right way for major countries to get along in the new era. Only by recognizing this can the true value of the summit be understood: it was not about a "deal" among major countries, but rather a new attempt by them to address differences through dialogue instead of confrontation. As long as all parties work toward the same goal and continue to act on the consensus reached, the seeds sown at the trilateral summit will eventually take root, sprout, bloom, and bear fruit. China stands ready to work with Russia and the U.S. to implement the consensus reached by the three leaders, continue to strengthen communication, meet global challenges, safeguard world peace and stability, and jointly make the world a better place. item.title: Addressing questions of our times and building a bright future together
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
Addressing questions of our times and building a bright future together On Nov. 18, Chinese President Xi Jinping delivered a keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong province. In his speech, Xi focused on the questions of our times: What is going on with the world? What should we do in the Asia-Pacific? To open doors or close doors, work together or against each other, adapt to change or stick to old ways? He offered a keen assessment of regional development trends and the progress of the times. He put forward China's proposals for building an Asia-Pacific community and bringing shared prosperity for all in the region, and reaffirmed China's commitment to sharing opportunities and pursuing common development with the Asia-Pacific and the wider world. His speech charted the course for Asia-Pacific cooperation under the new circumstances. The international landscape is marked by intertwined challenges and uncertainties. Global economic growth lacks momentum, while unilateralism and protectionism are rampant. At the same time, global trade continues to grow against headwinds, and breakthroughs are being made in emerging technologies at a faster pace, exerting a profound impact on global development. History has shown that openness brings progress, while isolation leads to backwardness. Born amid the waves of economic globalization, APEC has enabled the Asia-Pacific to steer the course of our times toward greater openness and connectivity. Drawing on this experience, Asia-Pacific economies should remain committed to openness and make fresh contributions to the world through more dynamic and resilient regional cooperation. In his speech, Xi put forward four proposals: upholding peace and stability, building bridges of opening up and cooperation, boosting innovation to drive growth, and expanding ways for mutual benefits and win-win outcomes. Together, they provide a clear action plan for building an Asia-Pacific community and promoting shared prosperity. There can be no prosperity without security, and no security without stability. All parties should resolve differences through dialogue and consultation, and overcome challenges through solidarity and cooperation. This is the way to cement the foundation for sustaining peace and stability in the Asia-Pacific. They should work steadily toward a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific (FTAAP) and build a multidimensional connectivity network to pave the way for greater economic integration in the Asia-Pacific. They should also forge science, technology, and innovation partnerships to turn strengths in innovation into drivers of growth, and provide strong impetus for economic growth in the Asia-Pacific. In addition, they should follow a people-centered development philosophy and strengthen economic and technical cooperation geared for developing economies, so that development fruits are shared by all economies and all groups and communities. Amid today's complex and volatile international environment, these four proposals provide the Asia-Pacific region with confidence and hope to stay on course and build consensus for cooperation. Bay area economies represent a promising new frontier for development. With their openness, connectivity and positive spillover effects, they serve as important vehicles for dynamic Asia-Pacific cooperation. The Asia-Pacific region is home to some of the world's most important bay areas. The Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area is one of China's most open and economically vibrant regions. The Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Guangzhou cluster, which has ranked first among the world's top 100 innovation clusters for two consecutive years, is a vivid example of how innovation and cooperation can drive regional development. China supports the establishment of a world association for bay areas economic cooperation and stands ready to deepen exchanges and interactions among bay areas with all parties and explore new ways for stronger economic cooperation in the Asia-Pacific, thus injecting fresh vitality into regional cooperation. This year marks the start of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) for economic and social development. The plan not only serves as a blueprint for China's own development, but also as a source of opportunities for economic growth in the Asia-Pacific and the wider world. It represents an invitation to cooperation that China has extended to business communities around the world. Drawing on the advantages of its super-sized open market and innovation testing ground, China will continue to increase imports of quality products and services and deepen integration between technological and industrial innovation, providing global business communities with a promising land for development. This year also marks the 25th anniversary of China's accession to the World Trade Organization (WTO). Over the past 25 years, China has remained committed to true multilateralism, fully honored its WTO accession commitments and steadily brought stability and predictability to world economic growth and international trade and economic cooperation. No matter how the international landscape may evolve, China will continue to expand high-standard opening up and stay firmly committed to high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, providing global business communities with an environment conducive to mutually beneficial cooperation. A China committed to openness and innovation will continue to work with all parties to write a new chapter of shared prosperity for the Asia-Pacific and the world. The Asia-Pacific is the common home of APEC economies, where all parties work together to pursue development and cooperation. China stands ready to join hands with its Asia-Pacific partners to address challenges facing development through opening up, generate momentum for growth through innovation, and pursue prosperity for all through cooperation. Together, they can build an Asia-Pacific community and create a brighter future for the region and the world. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: China's tech innovation engine powers a connected Asia-Pacific
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
China's tech innovation engine powers a connected Asia-Pacific An APEC-themed installation is seen on Xiangmihu road in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 15, 2026. (Xinhua/Jin Liwang) * China's push to unleash the potential of innovation and share technological dividends through open regional integration has resonated widely -- translating its innovation capacity into broader market opportunities and lending fresh momentum to economic growth and the building of an Asia-Pacific community. * Across the Asia-Pacific, China's technological innovations are finding applications in a growing range of industries and aspects of everyday life. * The release of the Shenzhen Initiative marked a milestone in the 30-year history of the APEC CEO Summit. It was a historic moment in Shenzhen, a city that has stood at the forefront of China's opening-up and has grown into a global innovation hub. BEIJING, Nov. 22 (Xinhua) -- As host of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China has placed openness, innovation and cooperation at the heart of its agenda as the three priority areas. Throughout this week's sessions, participants explored how the Asia-Pacific can navigate structural shifts and cultivate new engines of economic growth. China's push to unleash the potential of innovation and share technological dividends through open regional integration has resonated widely -- translating its innovation capacity into broader market opportunities and lending fresh momentum to economic growth and the building of an Asia-Pacific community. INNOVATION THAT BENEFITS ALL At an experimental durian orchard at Chiang Mai University in Thailand, agricultural lecturer Supakorn Wongsuk prepares a drone for takeoff. Having studied in China, he now applies the technology to explore more efficient methods of cultivating tropical fruits. Lifting smoothly into the air, the drone glides above rows of durian trees, releasing a fine mist of pesticide across their leaves and branches. "Using drones to spray pesticides can improve operational efficiency, reduce farmers' direct exposure to chemicals, and protect their health and safety," said Supakorn. He sees the Chinese innovations as offering benefits that extend well beyond farming efficiency. "For young people, drone operations can also create new job opportunities." Across the Asia-Pacific, China's technological innovations are finding applications in a growing range of industries and aspects of everyday life. The role of innovation also drew sharp focus at the APEC CEO Summit 2026 in Shenzhen. "Innovation is very important, and innovation cannot be done overnight. It requires strong education support and accumulated experience. This is where we think China can play a role," said Indonesian Chamber of Commerce and Industry Chairman Anindya N. Bakrie. "China has an important role to play," said Julien Leclair-Dionne, associate director at the University of Ottawa's Professional Development Institute. "Particularly given its technological capabilities, innovation ecosystem and experience in scaling emerging technologies." An AI trainer operates a robot to collect data at a humanoid robot innovation center in Wuhan, central China's Hubei Province, Nov. 11, 2026. (Xinhua/Wu Zhizun) "Ultimately, what matters most is not simply how advanced the technologies become, but how effectively the innovations are translated into opportunities for people, organizations and communities across the region," he said. OPENNESS CREATES OPPORTUNITIES Released on Wednesday, the Shenzhen Initiative of the APEC CEO Summit 2026 highlighted the transformative potential of frontier technologies such as artificial intelligence, while recognizing the accompanying risks and regulatory challenges that require coordinated regional oversight. At the heart of the document lies a clear, unified conviction among business leaders: no single economy can capture the promise of breakthrough technology -- or tame its disruptions -- alone; only deep regional cooperation can turn innovation into shared prosperity. Auckland Business Chamber CEO Simon Bridges emphasized the need for cooperation amid global uncertainty. "I think cooperation is probably the byword of APEC. And we know in the world right now, it's more important than ever," he said. China's approach to AI development provides "a very good example" that allows others to learn from its technological advances, he added. The appeal of Chinese AI models has become increasingly evident across the region. In South Korea, nearly half of the AI models released by local developers on Hugging Face, a globally popular open-source platform, between January and August this year were based on Chinese foundation models. "China has adopted AI with more open-weight, open-source, low-cost models that are going to be used by businesses around the world," said Jacob Cooke, CEO of WPIC Marketing + Technologies, a leading e-commerce and technology consultancy. "These Chinese companies have done their best to get this technology out to help people," Cooke said at the summit. The opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 is held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) The release of the Shenzhen Initiative marked a milestone in the 30-year history of the APEC CEO Summit. It was a historic moment in Shenzhen, a city that has stood at the forefront of China's opening-up and has grown into a global innovation hub. For Lee Ju-kwan, director of the National Center for APEC Studies at the Korea Institute for International Economic Policy of South Korea, Shenzhen's relentless innovation engine came vividly into focus during a visit to electric vehicle giant BYD's headquarters, offering a firsthand look at the homegrown tech muscle powering the city. "I was deeply impressed by what I saw, particularly robots performing tasks that would traditionally be carried out by human workers on the production line," Lee said. "This year, by hosting APEC, China has taken the opportunity to put forward and renew initiatives aimed at promoting openness and cooperation. I believe these efforts deserve attention and support," Lee said. GREEN INNOVATION "It's the most fantastic ride," said Jeffrey Sachs, a professor at Columbia University, looking back on an epic 15,000-km summer odyssey from Rome to China's Hong Kong, retracing Marco Polo's historic path behind the wheel of a BYD electric vehicle. This photo taken on Sept. 9, 2026 shows an assembly line at the BYD Fuzhou base in Fuzhou, east China's Jiangxi Province. (Xinhua/Wan Xiang) Sachs said the journey showed how far green technology had advanced. "The technology is already here. Most of it is in its most advanced stage in China," Sachs said during a high-level panel at the APEC CEO Summit 2026. He also noted that China had significantly reduced the cost of green technologies, making the transition more affordable. "To go green is not to make an extra burden for the sake of the planet. It's just to have a low-cost, resilient, state-of-the-art energy system," he said. The benefits of China's green innovation are also being felt by residents of Goulburn in New South Wales, Australia. With an integrated solar-and-storage solution supplied by a Chinese company, the local community has brought its own solar farm into operation. The facility began supplying electricity to the grid in March, with part of its annual profits to be channeled into a community fund to help residents facing energy poverty. "For a long time, it has been talk around the kitchen table. Suddenly here we are in amongst the panels, watching the sun send electrons to the people and my kids all own little parts of this with the community," said Goulburn resident Dave Suttle. "Without China's involvement, we definitely wouldn't have solar cells as cheap as now," Martin Green, Scientia Professor of Photovoltaic and Renewable Energy Engineering at the University of New South Wales, told Xinhua. Having worked with China's photovoltaic industry for more than four decades, Green is now collaborating with Chinese partners on the next generation of solar technology. "Working with China, we feel we're in a position to improve the solar performance more quickly," he said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

China's second homegrown large cruise ship begins maiden commercial voyage A tourist interacts with a robot on Adora Flora City, China's second domestically built large cruise ship, on Nov. 22, 2026. Adora Flora City embarked on its maiden voyage on Sunday, marking a new step in the country's efforts to expand cruise tourism and boost consumption. (Xinhua) GUANGZHOU, Nov. 22 (Xinhua) -- China's second domestically built large cruise ship, Adora Flora City, embarked on its maiden voyage on Sunday, marking a new step in the country's efforts to expand cruise tourism and boost consumption. Carrying more than 3,800 passengers, the ship departed from Guangzhou in south China's Guangdong Province on a six-day, five-night journey to Hong Kong and Hue, Vietnam. Measuring 341 meters in length and with a gross tonnage of 141,900, the vessel has 2,130 cabins and can accommodate up to 5,232 passengers. Construction of Adora Flora City began in August 2022. Operated by Adora Cruises under China Tourism Group, the ship was delivered in Shanghai, east China, on Nov. 6 and embarked on its first trial voyage on Nov. 9. Shi Dai, chairperson of China Tourism Group, said the company is using cruise operations to drive the development of integrated cultural tourism products and travel experiences, aiming to set a new benchmark for vacations at sea. Adora Flora City is larger and features a more streamlined design than its sister ship, Adora Magic City, China's first domestically built large cruise ship. Adora Magic City began commercial operations in January 2024 and has since completed about 250 voyages. Hu Zhenyu, deputy director of the Qianhai branch of the China Development Institute, said the entry into service of two domestically built large cruise ships marks a new phase for China's cruise industry. The development will not only expand the range of high-quality marine tourism products but also create new drivers of consumption in coastal areas, Hu said. In 2027, Adora Flora City is scheduled to undertake over 50 international voyages from its home port in Guangzhou, offering both short getaways and longer itineraries to destinations including Vietnam, Malaysia and Brunei. The ship will also offer voyages with no scheduled port calls, allowing passengers to enjoy the cruise ship as a destination in itself. The vessel departed from the Guangzhou Nansha International Cruise Home Port, one of China's largest integrated cruise port complexes. A duty-free store at the terminal also opened on Sunday, adding a fresh shopping option for cruise passengers. Wu Qingsong, deputy director of Guangzhou's culture, radio, television and tourism bureau, said the maiden voyage presents an opportunity for the city to better integrate its cruise port, shipping industry and tourism resources. Guo Jia, assistant vice president of product and guest experience at Adora Cruises, said the company plans to expand year-round operations across multiple home ports in east and north China, and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, offering passengers more high-quality cruise experiences. The maiden voyage comes as China seeks to expand tourism consumption. A 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) for cultural and tourism development calls for boosting spending on cruise and yacht tours, among other specialized tourism offerings. China has seen strong growth in cruise tourism, with total cruise passenger throughput rising 25.3 percent year on year in 2025, according to the Ministry of Natural Resources. Xi's speech marking 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth published (Xinhua) 16:47, November 23, 2026 BEIJING, Nov. 23 (Xinhua) -- A speech delivered by Chinese President Xi Jinping at a ceremony marking the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth has been published as a booklet. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the speech in Beijing on Nov. 12. The booklet, published by the People's Publishing House, is now available at Xinhua Bookstore outlets nationwide.
